hero.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget with $1.6 billion in vetoes hitting Indian River State College and local projects
hero.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed Florida's $117.6 billion state budget Monday in Tampa, using his line-item veto power to cut approximately $1.6 billion from the spending plan lawmakers approved. The budget takes effect July 1 and represents the fourth consecutive year DeSantis has reduced overall state spending through vetoes. The governor framed the action as fiscal responsibility, noting that Florida is one of few states actually cutting budgets rather than simply discussing it. He highlighted the state's roughly $18 billion in reserves and progress on debt reduction. "The debt has been cut in half, the reserves are good, the rainy day fund is flush," DeSantis said, adding that these are accomplishments "very few are able to actually accomplish."

The $1.6 billion in vetoes was distributed broadly across state priorities. About $800 million targeted direct line-item spending. Florida's corrections system faced some of the largest reductions, with tens of millions cut from prison repairs, new housing units, capital improvements, and pay adjustments. The governor argued that some corrections spending was tied to new debt he did not want the state to assume. Water and resiliency projects also took a significant hit, with more than $170 million cut from environment, water, agriculture, resiliency, and parks-related items. This included local stormwater, wastewater, flood mitigation, and infrastructure projects throughout Florida.

Education spending also experienced notable reductions. The vetoes included $15 million for Catholic school security alongside millions in cuts to college infrastructure and programs. Affected institutions included Palm Beach State College, College of the Florida Keys, Indian River State College, and Florida State University's College of Nursing. DeSantis said the final budget still funded major priorities including education, transportation, environmental restoration, law enforcement, and tax relief.

House Minority Leader Fentrice Driskell criticized the vetoes, claiming Democratic projects were cut at roughly twice the rate of Republican projects. She questioned the governor's priorities, suggesting he was more focused on cutting the budget than considering the people affected by the reductions. "What is this governor's priority?" Driskell asked. "Because he seems to be more obsessed with talking points and saying that he cut the budget rather than actually caring about the people who are going to be impacted by those cuts." DeSantis has previously stated that he considers lawmakers' support of his policy agenda when reviewing budget requests. Over eight years, DeSantis said his vetoes have totaled more than $10 billion, far exceeding cuts by recent predecessors combined.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce diver Greer Boyd identified after drowning near Fort Pierce Inlet
cards.teaser: A 63-year-old Fort Pierce man died Friday while attempting to recover a trolling motor that fell overboard near the Fort Pierce Inlet.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office has identified the diver found dead on Friday near the Fort Pierce Inlet as Greer Boyd, 63, of Fort Pierce. Investigators say Boyd was fishing with friends earlier in the day when the boat's trolling motor became detached and went overboard. The group returned to the area with diving equipment to attempt recovery of the motor. Boyd went into the water alone, and only his buoyancy compensator and air tank were located approximately 40 yards from the boat.

Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce received a Mayday call over VHF Channel 16 at approximately 11:30 a.m. Friday regarding a missing diver. Following the distress call, the Coast Guard notified the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, which immediately deployed four vessels to assist in the search. Martin County Fire Rescue Lt. Daniel DeGrazia, who was off-duty at the time, was able to assist and recovered the body of the missing diver at the bottom of the ocean in approximately 55 feet of water. An autopsy is scheduled today.

cards.headline: Woman, 78, killed after SUV rolls backward in Port St. Lucie driveway
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie woman died Sunday morning after an SUV parked in a residential driveway rolled backward and struck her.
cards.body:
A 78-year-old woman was killed Sunday morning after an SUV rolled backward and struck her in a residential driveway in Port St. Lucie, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The incident happened at approximately 10:47 a.m. when a 2016 Lincoln MKX SUV that was parked in the driveway began rolling backward while the woman was standing outside the vehicle near the open driver's door. The open door struck her, knocking her to the ground. Her adult son, 59, was in the passenger seat and had started the vehicle. The cause of the rollback remains under investigation. The woman was rushed to Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce, where she was pronounced deceased at 11:19 a.m.

Neighbor Daisy Cardona spoke about knowing the woman for several years and remembered her simple acts of kindness. "I saw the ambulance, the fire trucks, and two or three police cars. I felt sad, sad because I've known her for many years," Cardona said. "On Sundays, they would bring us bread, cupcakes, donuts, and sometimes cakes that were this big. May she rest in peace and my condolences to her family." The investigation remains ongoing.

Florida Highway Patrol reports the man was driving a Nissan Rogue SUV northbound when he approached a semi-truck with a trailer, also traveling in the outside lane. The Nissan collided with the back of the trailer.

cards.headline: Second fatal crash closes Florida's Turnpike in Stuart Monday

The closure impacted the turnpike in the Stuart area as authorities responded to the scene. The crash follows the earlier Monday morning fatality involving a Palm City man whose SUV struck a semi-truck at Mile Marker 136.

The series of fatal crashes over the four-day period has made it one of the deadliest stretches on Martin County roadways in recent memory.

cards.headline: 400-pound black bear killed after car collision on Southwest Martin Highway near Southwest Warfield Boulevard
cards.teaser: A 400-pound male black bear was killed Monday morning after being hit by a car on Southwest Martin Highway near Southwest Warfield Boulevard in Martin County.
cards.body:
A 400-pound male black bear was killed Monday morning after being struck by a car on Southwest Martin Highway near Southwest Warfield Boulevard, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Deputies responded after the motorist immediately stopped and called authorities. The driver told deputies the bear ran into the roadway before being struck by the vehicle. The driver was not injured, but the bear died at the scene.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office said the collision serves as a reminder of the wildlife present along rural Martin County roadways, particularly during early morning and evening hours when animals are most active. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission removed the bear from the scene. Traffic is now flowing normally through the area. This is the second bear sighting on the Treasure Coast this month, following a black bear that was caught on camera swimming through a waterway in the Town Park community of Port St. Lucie earlier in June.

cards.headline: Jupiter Fire Rescue deploys 2 firefighters to Venezuela earthquake relief mission
cards.teaser: Two Jupiter Fire Rescue firefighters deployed to Venezuela as part of a FEMA Urban Search and Rescue Task Force with less than 24 hours notice, joining crews from Delray Beach and Palm Beach County.
cards.body:
Jupiter Fire Rescue has deployed 2 firefighters to Venezuela as part of a FEMA Urban Search and Rescue Task Force providing earthquake relief. The firefighters are among a group of 80 first responders from Jupiter, Delray Beach, and Palm Beach County fire departments sent to assist with relief efforts. The crew was deployed with less than 24 hours notice and is expected to remain in Venezuela for at least two weeks.

The mission focuses on search and rescue operations in collapsed structures, including large buildings and smaller homes. The team brought heavy-duty equipment for breaking, cutting, breaching, and stabilization, along with technical rope rescue tools. Stephen Shaw, deputy fire chief of operations for Jupiter Fire Rescue, said the deployment reflects the department's commitment to helping those in need. Shaw noted that the experience and skills the firefighters practice during the deployment will benefit Jupiter Fire Rescue internally as the department continues to grow.

hero.headline: Boca Raton Independence Day Market Features Free Family Activities at City Hall July 4
hero.teaser: SoFlo Market founder Tatiana Freitas will host a free patriotic celebration at Boca Raton City Hall on Saturday, July 4, featuring a kids parade, DJ, vendors, and gourmet food.
hero.body:
The SoFlo Market will turn Boca Raton City Hall into a Fourth of July celebration Saturday, July 4, from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. Founder and organizer Tatiana Freitas told WPTV the event will feature a kids parade, a DJ, unique vendors, and gourmet food. The first 20 children through the gate will receive a free gift.

Family entertainment includes face painting, a foggy bubble station, mini golf, and balloon twisting alongside handmade crafts and desserts. The SoFlo Market's flamingo mascot will make a live appearance. Boca Raton firefighters and police officers have been invited to attend.

Kyle, Freitas' son, and Eddie, her husband, are part of the organizing team. Electricity will be powered by generators on-site. The event will take place at 201 West Palmetto Park Road with free admission. The markets run monthly, but Freitas said the Independence Day edition is always a standout.

cards.headline: Boca Raton's George Snow Scholarship Fund Awards Record $7.5 Million to 470 Students
cards.teaser: The George Snow Scholarship Fund distributed more than $7.5 million in scholarships and support services to 470 students across Palm Beach and Broward counties in 2026, marking a record year for the Boca Raton nonprofit.
cards.body:
The George Snow Scholarship Fund, headquartered in Boca Raton, awarded more than $7.5 million in scholarships and support services to 470 students across Palm Beach and Broward counties in 2026, President Tim Snow told WPTV. Founded over 40 years ago, the nonprofit has distributed more than $45 million to over 4,100 students, making it the largest scholarship provider in Palm Beach County. Snow said the program bridges the gap between traditional financial aid and what students and families can afford, offering four-year commitments to ensure stability throughout college.

Vice President of Development Jay Brandt noted that the fund's services extend beyond financial aid, providing mentorship, professional development, and resources like the College Compass podcast. One 2026 recipient, Zya Chow, a Wellington Community High School graduate, earned both the Royal Palm Hearing Aid Scholarship and the Davidowitz Family Caregiving Youth Scholarship and plans to attend Georgetown University. The Doyle-Whelchel Scholars Boutique, led by Scholar Services Coordinator Garvey Antoine, offers professional, formal, and casual wear so scholars can prepare for interviews, internships, and campus life. The boutique accepts donations of new or gently used clothing, footwear, and accessories.

cards.headline: Vero Beach MusicWorks Launches Fourteenth Concert Season to Expand Cultural Tourism
cards.body:
Vero Beach's MusicWorks has launched its fourteenth concert season, positioning Florida alongside California, Texas, New York, Tennessee, Georgia, Illinois, Nevada, Arizona, Michigan and Massachusetts in a multi-state cultural tourism initiative. The concert series aims to inspire multi-state travel and expand cultural tourism to the Treasure Coast.

The announcement was made Sunday as the organization unveiled plans for the upcoming season. MusicWorks has established itself as a regional cultural destination drawing visitors from across state lines.

The concert series represents a significant component of Vero Beach's arts and cultural programming. The organization's alignment with major cultural markets in ten other states reflects the growing recognition of the Treasure Coast as a destination for performing arts.

The fourteenth season continues MusicWorks' track record of bringing classical and contemporary performances to Indian River County. Concert schedules and ticket information will be released as the season progresses.

hero.headline: Florida extends digital evidence search warrant deadline to one year for child exploitation and serious crimes
hero.teaser: Ron DeSantis has signed legislation extending the amount of time law enforcement has to execute search warrants for digital evidence from 45 days to an entire year.
hero.body:
Governor Ron DeSantis has signed HB 359, legislation sponsored by Rep. Adam Anderson that extends the deadline for law enforcement to execute search warrants on encrypted phones, computers, and other digital devices from 45 days to one year. The new law is designed to modernize criminal justice procedures and provide law enforcement with realistic time frames to investigate digital evidence in cases involving child sexual abuse material, child exploitation, human trafficking, homicide, and other serious crimes where digital evidence is essential to securing convictions. Anderson said the change reflects modern realities in which digital devices are becoming more frequent tools of crime. "Protecting Florida's children and putting dangerous criminals behind bars should never be derailed by outdated laws that can't keep pace with modern technology," Anderson said.

The legislation builds on reforms enacted following the 2023 Moschella v. State decision. Law enforcement agencies across the state argued that the previous 45-day deadline remained inadequate due to increasingly sophisticated encryption technology, limited forensic resources, and significant laboratory backlogs. State Attorney Bruce Bartlett, who serves in Pinellas County, praised the bill, noting that the volume of child sexual abuse material law enforcement investigates has risen exponentially. The new law gives law enforcement adequate time to access digital evidence without making repeated extension requests on existing warrants, reducing unnecessary court proceedings. It does not expand authority to seize devices or create new search powers for law enforcement.

cards.body:
Ron DeSantis vetoed at least $13.7 million in Pinellas County area projects from the new state budget, with the largest local cuts affecting elder care, hurricane hardening, animal welfare, public safety and flood control. The vetoes were included in DeSantis' June 29 budget transmittal, where he agreed to a $117.6 billion budget after more than $1.6 billion in vetoes statewide. The largest local cut was tied to the Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly, or PACE, with DeSantis vetoing two expansion items that would have funded 300 new slots in the county. One veto struck nearly $591,000 for 50 new PACE slots at a Pinellas County organization owned and operated by Habitat Healthcare LLC or an affiliate, effective April 1, 2027. Another cut was just over $3.9 million for 250 new PACE slots at a Pinellas County organization owned and operated by Kinship Health or a subsidiary, effective March 1, 2027. In all, DeSantis vetoed more than $30.6 million in PACE appropriations requests statewide.

The next-largest Pinellas-area vetoes were two separate $2 million projects: one for the Pinellas County Lealman Exchange Hurricane Hardening project and another for Friends of Strays Dog Adoption Center construction. DeSantis also vetoed several local stormwater, drainage and transportation-related projects, including $1 million for Clearwater's Elevate Bayshore project, $1 million for the Madeira Beach Area 6 Roadway Improvement Project, $750,000 for Tampa Bay Watch Shoreline Protection and Water Quality Improvements, $600,000 for the Largo Allen's Creek Flood Mitigation Project, and $500,000 for St. Petersburg Childs Park Storm Drainage Improvements. Public safety cuts included $350,000 for a St. Petersburg Police Department K-9 facility, $500,000 for a Redington Beaches Fire Suppression Unit, and $160,000 for Safety Harbor City Hall security improvements.

cards.headline: Hillsborough County loses more than $8.2 million to Governor's vetoes, including advanced metering and flood relief
cards.teaser: Ron DeSantis has vetoed more than $8.2 million from the budget for Hillsborough County, including cuts to an advanced metering project, flood relief, a scholarship readiness pilot and more.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis vetoed more than $8.2 million in funding for Hillsborough County projects from the Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget. His largest veto was a $2 million funding item from Sen. Michael Owen for advanced metering infrastructure in the county. Advanced metering provides utility users with more accurate usage information and the ability to monitor for water leaks. The $2 million was the full funding request and would have covered a small portion of an overall $30 million project affecting about 15,000 residents. DeSantis also slashed $1.5 million for a flood relief project on South Howard Avenue, where flooding is prevalent, which had been requested by Karen Gonzalez Pittman. Nearly $879,000 earmarked for a Hillsborough County Schools pilot program to enhance Bright Futures scholarship eligibility and readiness, requested by Rep. Traci Koster, was also cut. The funds would have supported a pilot project with SchoolLinks, a platform offering real-time scholarship eligibility tracking.

Additional vetoes included $800,000 from the Children's Network of Hillsborough's CHANCE program supporting victims of human trafficking and $750,000 from Tampa Bay Watch for shoreline protection and water quality improvements. DeSantis also cut $675,000 for a fallen firefighters memorial and $260,000 for Hillsborough County Fire Rescue emergency management. Other vetoed items included $500,000 for intersection improvements at 30th Street and Sligh Avenue in Tampa, $265,000 for an AMSkills accelerator program for trades education, $250,000 for Hillsborough College's artificial intelligence program, and $200,000 for University of South Florida neuromusculoskeletal research.

cards.headline: Jay Collins sues to remove James Fishback from Florida Governor's race over residency requirement
cards.teaser: Gubernatorial candidate Jay Collins filed a lawsuit challenging GOP Primary opponent James Fishback's eligibility for office, arguing Fishback does not meet a seven-year Florida residency requirement.
cards.body:
Gubernatorial candidate Jay Collins filed a lawsuit in Leon County Circuit Court challenging GOP Primary opponent James Fishback's eligibility for office, arguing he does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement. The legal complaint notes that Fishback registered to vote in Washington, D.C., in November 2020 and voted in city elections, requiring him to establish legal residency in the District of Columbia and declare he did not claim voting residence in any other state or territory, including Florida. The lawsuit documents that Fishback later purchased a home in Washington and claimed it as his principal residence to receive a homestead tax deduction. According to documents filed with the lawsuit, he still claimed that deduction as recently as February 2024. Though Fishback corrected the form in April, requiring additional tax payments and penalties, the lawsuit argues this does not resolve whether he maintained Florida residency for the required seven-year period before running for Governor.

Collins, Florida's current Lieutenant Governor, also named Secretary of State Cord Byrd as a plaintiff, contending the Division of Elections should not have granted Fishback qualified candidate status earlier this month. The lawsuit alleges Fishback made false statements on his candidate oath. Collins said the law must be enforced before voters receive ballots for the Republican Primary in August. Eleven Republicans have qualified for Governor this year, including U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner. Fishback, who lists Madison as his current residence, claims he is a fourth-generation Floridian and has repeatedly shown driver's licenses to verify his Florida residency. Collins has requested an expedited hearing on whether Fishback should be removed from the ballot.

cards.headline: DeSantis vetoes hundreds of millions in corrections funding tied to new prison hospital construction
cards.teaser: Ron DeSantis has vetoed millions in funding for Department of Corrections capital improvement projects and pay increases, calling the approach a D.C. swamp tactic.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis has vetoed HB 5403E, legislation sponsored by Okaloosa County Republican Rep. Patt Maney that passed both chambers unanimously in May. The bill would have funded $50 million annually in corrections capital projects for 40 years and mandated construction of a new 600-bed corrections hospital in Gilchrist County using bond funding. The veto also eliminates $226.5 million in contingent corrections funding, including a $91.5 million pay increase for Department of Corrections employees that would have raised the minimum correctional officer base pay to $24 an hour. Other eliminated contingent funding included capital improvement projects, inmate job training and employment skills programs, reentry programs, and $1 million for an employee retention plan.

In his veto letter, DeSantis said he had proposed a $374 million pay increase for correctional officers but argued against tying pay raises to debt obligations for a new prison hospital. "This is a D.C. swamp approach to correctional pay, attempting to force the state to take on new debt to build a prison hospital by holding hostage pay increases for our hard-working correctional officers. This is not a game I am willing to play," DeSantis wrote. Department of Corrections Secretary Ricky Dixon has previously called for higher officer salaries, noting Florida lags behind neighboring states. In April, Dixon said Alabama pays officers $35 an hour after 18 months, compared to Florida's proposed $24 an hour.

cards.headline: Miami-Dade Schools secure $1 million for AI gun detection while other Florida counties lose funding
cards.teaser: A million-dollar artificial intelligence project aimed at keeping guns out of Miami-Dade schools escaped the Governor's veto pen, but three small-dollar appropriations to do the same in other counties were cut.
cards.body:
Ron DeSantis signed the 2026-27 state budget after slashing $1.7 billion, including $810 million worth of projects and another $900 million in contingent spending authority. Among the casualties were three procurements for an AI-backed school safety service developed by ZeroEyes, a Pennsylvania-based company that markets firearm detection software that piggybacks onto CCTV systems already wired into schools. Lawmakers filed numerous local funding requests for the platform ranging from $15,000 to $3 million. Only four projects survived the appropriations process: Franklin received $15,000, Hernando received $240,000, Seminole received $250,000, and Miami-Dade received $1 million rather than the $3 million originally sought in requests filed by Sen. Shevrin Jones and Rep. Kevin Chambliss.

Founded in 2018 by former Navy SEALs and technology executives following the Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School shooting, ZeroEyes uses "cutting-edge video analytics" to detect guns. Every detection is immediately reviewed by a person before alerts are sent to school officials or law enforcement. The company said it had made more than 1,000 verified detections across all monitored sites since the platform's full rollout in 2023. The platform does not use facial recognition technology nor store biometric identifiers. According to the Miami-Dade funding request, the district previously piloted the technology and sought state assistance to deploy it systemwide, with ZeroEyes required to report total detections on campuses as a performance measure.

hero.headline: Palm City man dies after SUV collides with semi-truck on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County
hero.body:

Florida Highway Patrol reports the man was driving a Nissan Rogue SUV northbound when he approached a semi-truck with a trailer, also traveling in the outside lane. The Nissan collided with the back of the trailer.

The Palm City driver was transported to Florida Coast Medical Center where he was pronounced dead at 1:55 a.m. The driver of the semi-truck was not injured in the collision.

Florida Highway Patrol is investigating the crash. The incident marks one of multiple fatal traffic crashes in Martin County over recent days.

cards.headline: 78-year-old woman killed when SUV rolls backward in Port St. Lucie driveway
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie woman died Sunday morning after a 2016 Lincoln MKX SUV rolled backward and struck her in a residential driveway.
cards.body:
A 78-year-old woman was killed Sunday morning after an SUV rolled backward in a residential driveway in Port St. Lucie. The incident occurred at approximately 10:47 a.m. when a 2016 Lincoln MKX began rolling backward while the woman was standing outside the vehicle near the open driver's door. The open door struck her, knocking her to the ground. Her 59-year-old son, who was sitting in the passenger seat, had started the vehicle. The woman was transported to Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce, where she was pronounced deceased at 11:19 a.m. The cause of the rollback remains under investigation by the Florida Highway Patrol.

Neighbors who knew the woman for several years spoke about her kindness and generosity. Daisy Cardona, a neighbor, recalled witnessing the emergency response and expressed her sadness over the loss. "On Sundays, they would bring us bread, cupcakes, donuts, and sometimes cakes," Cardona said. "May she rest in peace and my condolences to her family." The Florida Highway Patrol continues to investigate the incident.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce diver dies attempting to recover trolling motor from ocean floor
cards.teaser: The St.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office has identified Greer Boyd, 63, of Fort Pierce as the diver found dead Friday near the Fort Pierce Inlet. Boyd was fishing with friends earlier in the day when the boat's trolling motor became detached and went overboard. The group returned to the area with diving equipment to recover the motor. Boyd entered the water alone, and only his buoyancy compensator and air tank were located approximately 40 yards from the boat.

The Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce received a Mayday call over VHF Channel 16 at approximately 11:30 a.m. Friday regarding the missing diver. Following the distress call, the Coast Guard notified the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, which deployed four vessels to assist in the search. Martin County Fire Rescue Lt. Daniel DeGrazia, who was off-duty at the time, assisted in the recovery effort and recovered Boyd's body at the bottom of the ocean in approximately 55 feet of water. An autopsy is scheduled. The incident remains under investigation by the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office and the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission.
